OneModifierComposite One-modifier composite — combines a modifier binding and a main binding; outputs true only when both are pressed simultaneously. QuaternionComposite Quaternion composite — combines three float axis bindings (x/y/z Euler angles in degrees) into a UnityEngine.Quaternion. TwoModifiersComposite Two-modifiers composite — combines two modifier bindings and a main binding; outputs true only when all three are pressed simultaneously. Vector2DComposite 2D vector composite — combines four boolean directional bindings (up/down/left/right) into a normalized UnityEngine.Vector2. Define which source axes map to Unity's Right/Up/Forward to convert between coordinate systems. Uses direct matrix transformation: For Vector3: v' = C * v (where C is the conversion matrix) For Quaternion: M' = C * M * C^T (similarity transform on rotation matrix) The conversion matrix and its transpose are computed once on first use and cached for performance. index.html.summary: VotanicXR2 Documentation VotanicXR2 is a Unity toolkit for XR apps that run on HMDs and Votanic CAVE / dome systems. It extends Unity XR Interaction Toolkit (XRI) rather than replacing it. Core components — such as interactables, interactors, and locomotion providers — remain native to XRI, while VotanicXR2 introduces input mapping, CAVE configurations, faders and additional APIs to control interactors and locomotion providers. tutorials/input-system/input-action-map-.summary: Input action map editor The Input Action Map Editor allows you to define "Actions" (such as Grab, Teleport, or Menu) and bind them to specific hardware inputs across different controller profiles. Navigate to the top menu in the Unity Editor and select VXR Input > Action Map Editor to open the editor. Configure input action map To create a new action map, select New from top right corner of the context menu. To load an existing action map, select Load from top right corner of the context menu. To save an existing action map, select Save from top right corner of the context menu. To save an existing action map as a brand new copy, select Save As from top right corner of the context menu. Configure actions To create a new action, select the blue Add (+) icon in the header of action map structure column. To reorder an existing action, select the Up (↑) or Down (↓) Arrow icon of the action. To delete an existing action, select the Cross (✖) icon of the action. Edit action properties If you select an action, you can edit its properties in the Details panel on the right: Action Type Description Every Frame Called every frame On Value Change Called when the input value changes Configure bindings To add a new binding, select the green Add (+) icon of the action. To delete an existing binding, select the Cross (✖) icon of the binding. If you select a binding, you can edit its properties in the Details panel on the right: Edit composite bindings Like Unity's input system, VotanicXR2 also support composite bindings. Refer to Composite bindings to learn more. To add a new composite binding, select the green Add (+) icon of the action, and select the composite binding type from the popup menu. To edit the properties of a composite part, click on the composite part and use the Details panel on the right to edit its properties. Edit control schemes Input action assets can have multiple control schemes, which let you enable or disable different sets of bindings for your actions for different types of devices. To add a new control scheme, select Manage then Add New Control Scheme from the control scheme section. To change the control scheme of a binding, select Change then select the control scheme from the popup menu. To delete a control scheme, select Manage then select the control scheme from the popup menu. Set the active action map or config file To change the the input action map used by your project, follow these steps: Select VXR SDK Manager in the hierarchy. Go to VXR SDK Manager component: To set the active config of the project, click Select Config and pick the .vxrc2 config file. To set the active action map of the project, click Select Action Map and pick the .json action map file. Save the scene or apply the changes. Set the active control scheme Once you set an action map in the input manager, you can enable or disable the sets of bindings to use by configuring the active control scheme: To actively test your XR application during development, enable the control scheme that matches your testing hardware and environment. These control schemes are provided in the default action map: PC control scheme for local PC testing HMD control scheme for Head-mounted display testing CAVE control scheme for testing in Votanic CAVE systems

tutorials/input-system/link-action-to-me.summary: Link up action to in-code methods This section explains how to connect actions defined in the Input Action Map Editor to your XR game logic using the VXRActionBinding class. By utilizing this class, you can bind specific in-code methods to input actions, enabling your scripts to automatically listen for and respond whenever those actions are triggered in runtime. To link an action to in-code method, follow these steps: Set up an action in the Input Action Map Editor Initialize a VXRActionBinding using the exact action name from the editor and bind the action to a compatible method Set the .Bound property of the binding to true to activate it Code example: Call method on every button press Before you begin to write the script, you must define an action within the Input Action Map Editor. Open the editor via VXR Input > Action Map Editor, create the action and save the changes to the action map. The following script demonstrates the implementation pattern for linking a "Fire" action to print a custom debug message. using UnityEngine; using Votanic.VXR2.Core.Input; public class SampleGunObject : MonoBehaviour { // Action name defined in the input action map editor private readonly string fireActionName = "Fire"; // Action binding private VXRActionBinding<bool> _fireAction; IEnumerator Start() { yield return new WaitUntil(() => VXRObjectManager.Instance.Initialized); // Initialize an action binding _fireAction = new VXRActionBinding<bool>(fireActionName, OnFireAction); } // Enable / disable / dispose the action binding to reduce cost from input manager void OnEnable() { if (_fireAction != null) _fireAction.Bound = true; } void OnDisable() { if (_fireAction != null) _fireAction.Bound = false; } void OnDestroy() { if (_fireAction != null) _fireAction.Dispose(); } // Implement method private void OnFireAction(bool isPressed) { if (isPressed) { Debug.Log("Fire action: button pressed"); } else { Debug.Log("Fire action: button released"); } } }

tutorials/interaction/interactor-setting.summary: Configure interactor settings In VotanicXR2 SDK, each hand controller can have one or more interactor components (from Unity XR Interaction Toolkit) attached to them that allow player to interact with the virtual world. By default, the SDK provides two hand controller settings (both left and right) plus a set of default interactor settings to help kickstart your project. Set the active hand controller setting Select VXR SDK Manager > VXR Object Manager in the hierachy. In the inspector, go to VXR Object Manager component, click either the Left Hand Controller Setting or Right Hand Controller Setting field and assign a VXRHandControllerSetting ScriptableObject to set the active hand controller setting. Edit hand controller properties If you select a VXRHandControllerSetting ScriptableObject, you can edit its properties in the Inspector tab: To set the visual prefab, select a reference in the Visual Prefab field To edit the interactors attached to hand controller, select a VXRInteractorSetting reference and add them to the Interactor Settings list. Edit interactor properties If you select a VXRInteractorSetting ScriptableObject, you can edit its properties in the Inspector tab: To set the interactor prefab, select a reference in the Interactor Prefab field. To enable / disable the interactor on start, tick / untick Enable On Start. To enable / disable the interactor to support base input, tick / untick Enable Base Input. To enable / disable the interactor to support UI input, tick / untick Enable UI Input. Create custom hand controller or interactor setting Right click on your Project window to open the context menu Go to Create > Votanic XR 2. Select either VXRHandControllerSetting or VXRInteractorSetting to create a custom hand controller or interactor setting. tutorials/interaction/using-interactors..title: Using interactors | VotanicXR2 Documentation
tutorials/interaction/using-interactors..summary: Using interactors To customize behavior of existing interactors, VotanicXR2 allows developers to manually control interactors under player entities which is accessed through VXRPlayer.Players.First().RightController.ControllerHandler. Interactor control API The VXRHandControllerHandler class provides the following methods to control the interactors under player entities. VXRHandControllerHandler Public Methods Method Description GetInteractors Returns a collection of all interactors registered to the entity. GetInteractorByName Retrieves a specific interactor by its GameObject name. Returns null if not found. IsInteractorActive Checks if an interactor is active by name or if a specific interactor instance is active. Returns false if the interactor is missing. SetInteractorActive Enables or disables an interactor. ResetInteractors Disables all interactors and clears the interaction group. RegisterActiveInteractor Register an interactor that was not created from VXRHandControllerSetting. UnregisterActiveInteractor Unregister an interactor previously added with RegisterActiveInteractor or created from settings. Code example: Press button to cycle through interactors This example demonstrates how to implement cycling through a bunch of interactors when you press a button. using System.Collections; using System.Collections.Generic; using System.Linq; using System.Reflection; using UnityEngine; using UnityEngine.XR.Interaction.Toolkit.Interactors; using Votanic.VXR2.Core; using Votanic.VXR2.Core.Input; using Votanic.VXR2.Core.Player; namespace Votanic.VXR2.Sample { /// <summary> /// Cycles the right-hand interactors, including one registered at runtime outside of /// <see cref="VXRHandControllerSetting"/>. /// Assign <see cref="sampleInteractor"/> in the inspector (a scene object with XRBaseInteractor). /// </summary> public class InteractorControl : MonoBehaviour { private readonly string triggerActionName = "NextInteractor"; [SerializeField] [Tooltip("Optional interactor that is not listed in the hand controller setting. Registered at runtime onto the right controller.")] private XRBaseInteractor sampleInteractor; private VXRActionBinding<bool> _buttonInput; private List<XRBaseInteractor> interactors; private int index = -1; private VXRHandControllerHandler controllerHandler; private bool sampleInteractorRegistered; IEnumerator Start() { yield return new WaitUntil(() => VXRObjectManager.Instance.Initialized); _buttonInput = new VXRActionBinding<bool>(triggerActionName, ButtonAction); controllerHandler = VXRPlayer.Players.First().RightController.ControllerHandler; // Access controller handler of current player if (sampleInteractor != null) { controllerHandler.RegisterActiveInteractor(sampleInteractor, true); sampleInteractorRegistered = true; } interactors = controllerHandler.GetInteractors().ToList(); // Get list of interactor attached to the controller controllerHandler.ResetInteractors(); MoveToNextInteractor(); } private void OnEnable() { if (_buttonInput != null) _buttonInput.Bound = true; } private void OnDisable() { if (_buttonInput != null) _buttonInput.Bound = false; } private void OnDestroy() { if (sampleInteractorRegistered && controllerHandler != null && sampleInteractor != null) { controllerHandler.UnregisterActiveInteractor(sampleInteractor); sampleInteractorRegistered = false; } if (_buttonInput != null) _buttonInput.Dispose(); } private void ButtonAction(bool value) { if (value) MoveToNextInteractor(); } private void MoveToNextInteractor() { if (interactors == null || interactors.Count == 0) return; index++; index %= interactors.Count; controllerHandler.ResetInteractors(); controllerHandler.SetInteractorActive(interactors[index], true); } } }

tutorials/locomotion/default-locomotion-.title: Default locomotion providers | VotanicXR2 Documentation
tutorials/locomotion/default-locomotion-.summary: Default locomotion providers VotanicXR2 provides a set of built-in locomotion tools to help user navigate in the virtual world. Each player have a set of locomotion provider components (from Unity XR Interaction Toolkit) attached to them that allow them to move in different ways. The player in VotanicXR2 by default has a list of interactors attached to it. For the related controls, refer to default input mappings. Locomotion providers Locomotion provider Description Turn XRI locomotion provider that handles user rotation. Modified to disable the 180-degree XRI snap turn. Move XRI locomotion provider that handles user movement. Modified to determine the forward direction based on which hand (left or right) is currently available. Head Provided by VXR2 framework. Recall Provided by VXR2 framework. Teleport Provided by VXR2 framework. Gravity XRI locomotion provider that handles user gravity. Grab XRI locomotion provider that allows the user to move with one hand as if grabbing the whole world around them. Tip Customize locomotion button mappings in the Action Map Editor. Gravity locomotion special behavior when flying VotanicXR2 provides a flying action for user to vertically move up and down along the scene. To allow fly action to run smoothly for users, VotanicXR2 SDK modifies the gravity locomotion provider in runtime. The modification leads to four movement mode and some special behavior on how the gravity locomotion provider act when you run your scene, as summarized by the table below: Specifically, the user gravity is temporarily disabled when the user is flying with gravity on. User Gravity User Gravity ON User Gravity OFF Fly When Flying Does not fall until stop flying (User gravity disabled when flying) Free flying When Not Flying Normal walking, does fall Normal walking, does not fall

tutorials/locomotion/using-locomotion-pr.title: Using locomotion providers | VotanicXR2 Documentation
tutorials/locomotion/using-locomotion-pr.summary: Using locomotion providers To customize behavior of existing locomotion providers, VotanicXR2 allows developers to manually control locomotion providers under player entities which is accessed through VXRPlayer.Players.First().LocomotionWrapper. Locomotion control API The VXRLocomotionWrapper class provides the following methods for controlling locomotion providers of a player. VXRLocomotionWrapper Public Methods Method Description GetLocomotionProviders Retrieves all locomotion providers of player. GetActiveLocomotionProviders Retrieves all active locomotion providers of player. GetLocomotionProvider Retrieves a locomotion provider of the specified type from the player. Returns null if a locomotion provider of that type is not found. RegisterLocomotionProvider Add the specified locomotion provider to player's LocomotionMediator. UnregisterLocomotionProvider Remove the specified locomotion provider from player's LocomotionMediator. Code example: Press button to toggle locomotion providers This example demonstrates how to implement toggling the locomotion providers when you press a button. using System.Collections; using System.Collections.Generic; using System.Linq; using UnityEngine; using UnityEngine.XR.Interaction.Toolkit.Locomotion; using Votanic.VXR2.Core.Input; using Votanic.VXR2.Core.Locomotion; using Votanic.VXR2.Core; public class SampleLocomotionController : MonoBehaviour { private readonly string triggerActionName = "NextLocomotionProvider"; private VXRActionBinding<bool> _buttonAction; private List<LocomotionProvider> locomotionProviders; private bool enableLocomotion = true; private VXRLocomotionWrapper locomotionWrapper; IEnumerator Start() { yield return new WaitUntil(() => VXRObjectManager.Instance.Initialized); _buttonAction = new VXRActionBinding<bool>(triggerActionName, ButtonAction); // Access locomotion wrapper of current player locomotionWrapper = VXRPlayer.Players.First().LocomotionWrapper; // Get all locomotion providers from locomotion wrapper locomotionProviders = locomotionWrapper.GetLocomotionProviders.ToList(); } private void OnEnable() { if (_buttonAction != null) _buttonAction.Bound = true; } private void OnDisable() { if (_buttonAction != null) _buttonAction.Bound = false; } private void OnDestroy() { if (_buttonAction != null) _buttonAction.Dispose(); } private void ButtonAction(bool value) { if (value) ToggleLocomotionProviders(); } private void ToggleLocomotionProviders() { enableLocomotion = !enableLocomotion; if (enableLocomotion) { foreach (LocomotionProvider provider in locomotionProviders) { locomotionWrapper.RegisterLocomotionProvider(provider); } } else { foreach (LocomotionProvider provider in locomotionProviders) { locomotionWrapper.UnregisterLocomotionProvider(provider); } } } }

tutorials/project-setup/getting-started..title: Getting Started | VotanicXR2 Documentation
tutorials/project-setup/getting-started..summary: Getting Started with VotanicXR2 This guide describes the initial setup of the VotanicXR2 SDK. By the end of this page, you will have a configured Unity project with core VotanicXR2 features initialized and ready for development. Prerequisites Before importing the SDK, ensure your development environment meets the following requirements: Unity Version: Unity 6000.0.82f1 LTS or newer Render Pipeline: Universal Render Pipeline Create new Unity project Choose a compatible Unity editor version, such as Unity 6000.0.82f1 LTS For your chosen Unity version, select the Universal 3D template when you create new project. Import SDK unitypackage When you import the VotanicXR2 SDK, the following packages are also installed automatically as dependecies: XR Hands: 1.7.3 or newer XR Interaction Toolkit: 3.2.2 or newer To import the VotanicXR2 SDK package into your project: Select Window > Package Manager. In the Package Manager, select the + button and choose Install package from git URL. Copy and paste the SDK git url (https://github.com/VOTANIC/VotanicXR2-SDK-Unity.git?path=/Unity6) into the text box then click Install. Unity will automatically fetch and install the SDK for the project. Set up the Unity scene At a minimum, a scene needs the following to work with VXR2 SDK: VXR SDK Manager VXR Start Point You can either set up the scene by: Using one of the provided sample scene, or Creating a new scene and manually add in the required components Start with a sample scene To set up a proper VXR2 scene, go into or duplicate one of the sample scenes and modify them to suit your project need. Start with a new scene To set up a proper VXR2 scene using a new scene, do the followings: Create a new Unity scene. In the hierarchy, right-click and select Votanic XR 2 > Spawn SDK Manager and then select Votanic XR 2 > Spawn Start Point. You should see both the VXR SDK Manager and VXR Start Point spawned within the project. Select VXR Start Point in the hierarchy and place it to where the user should appear in the scene. Set up project config and action map Download the default .vxr2 project config and .json action map from default resources folder on SDK github page. Place the downloaded files under StreamingAssets folder in the project hierarchy. Select VXR SDK Manager in the hierarchy. Go to VXR SDK Manager component: To set the active config of the project, click Select Config and pick the .vxrc2 config file. To set the active action map of the project, click Select Action Map and pick the .json action map file. Configure project settings Navigate to the top menu and select Edit > Project Settings.... Select Votanic > VXR2 category. Click on both Use Votanic VXR2 Render Pipeline Asset and Disable DXGI to apply the settings. Navigate to XR Plug-in Management. Tick OpenXR checkbox. Activate the license key Launch the VotanicXR Suite and select License Manager. Select Activate on the bottom-left corner. Input license key in the textbox then press Activation. The newly activated license will be shown in the App List. Verify installation To verify that VotanicXR2 SDK and its dependencies are configured correctly, do the followings: Click Play button at the top of Unity Editor to run the scene. Test the default controls: For PC: WASD to move, Mouse to look, Space to select For HMD: LS to move, RS to snap turn, Right Trigger to select Next steps Now that you have verified your setup, you can begin building your XR projects with other SDK features: Interaction Framework: Understanding Interactors and Interactables Locomotion: Setting up Teleportation and Smooth Movement VXR2 Input System: Customizing Action Maps

tutorials/project-setup/overview.html.title: Overview | VotanicXR2 Documentation
tutorials/project-setup/overview.html.summary: Overview VotanicXR2 is a development toolkit for XR applications on Unity. Projects built with it can run on HMDs and on Votanic CAVE / dome systems without rewriting interaction logic for each platform. Extended from Unity XRI: The SDK is built as an extension of the Unity XR Interaction Toolkit (XRI) framework. Developers can utilize native Unity XRI features alongside the VotanicXR2 toolkit. Specialized for CAVE & Cross-platform: VotanicXR2 features are specialized and optimized for Votanic CAVE system. XR Projects built with the SDK can function across supported platforms, including HMDs and CAVEs. Check out Getting Started to start building your project with the VotanicXR2 SDK.
